details:
LUNAVIS AI: Intelligent Lunar Landing-Site Analysis Platform

LUNAVIS AI is an intelligent lunar landing-site analysis platform designed to support the identification and evaluation of potential landing locations near the Moon's south pole. The project addresses one of the major challenges of lunar exploration: finding locations that provide safe terrain conditions while offering favorable environmental conditions for sustained robotic and future human missions.

The platform combines lunar surface and terrain information with quantitative indicators, including solar illumination duration, Earth visibility, terrain slope, and elevation. These indicators are used to evaluate and compare candidate landing locations. By analyzing the surrounding topography, LUNAVIS AI aims to help users understand how mountains, crater rims, and other geological features influence sunlight exposure, surface accessibility, and communication visibility with Earth.

The system is designed around a data-driven analytical approach. Users can examine candidate locations, visualize their characteristics, and compare their suitability using measurable parameters. For example, an illustrative site profile may display 65% estimated Earth visibility, a terrain slope of 5°, and an elevation of 120 meters. These values are hypothetical demonstrations rather than verified lunar measurements.

Benefits and Intended Impact

LUNAVIS AI aims to make complex lunar datasets more accessible and understandable through an integrated analytical and visualization platform. Its potential benefits include:

  • Supporting preliminary identification and comparison of candidate lunar landing locations.
  • Improving understanding of the relationship between lunar topography, solar illumination, and Earth
